newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Eltin sees 2nd half net matching 1st half.
newsitem.headline: Eltin sees 2nd half net matching 1st half.

text.p: Mining contractor Eltin Ltd said on Wednesday it now expects net profit before abnormals for the second half to June 30 to be similar to that of the first half after problems with contracts in Chile and Western Australia.
When reporting its first half results in mid-February, Eltin had said it expected a higher second half profit.
In the first half ended December 31, Eltin posted a net profit of A$6.33 million after an abnormal profit of A$230,000.
But in 1995/96, it made a net loss of A$8.15 million after a A$25 million abnormal loss mainly on write-downs of 51 percent-owned French gold miner, Mines d'Or de Salsigne SA.

Eltin said production at the Refugio gold mine in Chile had been closed since June 10 after abnormally heavy snowfalls cut access to the mine although it expected production to resume within the next 15 days.
Under the Refugio agreement with the client, the company was allowed some compensation in these circumstances, it said.
The benefits expected from improvements in Eltin's mobile equipment and the client's crushing plant as foreshadowed earlier this year had not flowed through as quickly as expected.
This combined, with the effects of the snow, will result in a significant loss for the site in 1996/97, Eltin said.
But recent management changes and improved operating performance should result in a better financial performance in 1997/98, Eltin said.

"Eltin is committed to building a critical mass in Chile and the experience of operating at sites like Refugio, some 4,400 metres (14,400 feet) above sea level, will place the company in a good position for future contracts," it said.

In Australia, performance of the Mt Leyshon gold mining contract has deteriorated in the last four months and the A$4 million provision raised last year will not be enough to cover expected losses which will hit 1996/97 earnings, it said.
Eltin said all other operations in Australia and New Zealand continue to operate satisfactorily notwithstanding heavy rainfall in Western Australia in the previous five months.
"Overall it is now expected that the group's second half result, before abnormals, will be similar to the first half," it said.
"Changes in management in Chile, the completion of the Mt Leyshon contract in 1997/98 and the commencement of new contracts should result in an improved performance in 1997/98," it added.
